issues.body: `backfill_workflow_seam_report()` checks the backfill step's conditionality, but it never checks the `targets` job or its `resolve` step for an `if:` condition. Adding `if: false` to either is valid workflow YAML and prevents the matrix output from being produced; the dependent backfill job is then skipped, yet all newly added shipped-shape assertions still pass. The mutant table likewise has no deleted/inert experiment for these controls. This is the exact fail-silent YAML seam the change says it covers.
issues.fix_hint: Report and assert that the `targets` job and the policy-resolving step are executable under the intended events (including explicit absence/exact value of any `if:`). Add non-crashing mutants that make each condition inert and verify a named finding changes while the complete self-test row count is preserved.
issues.title: The target resolver can be disabled with `if: false` without failing the self-test

issues.body: `targets_policy_sourced` is true when the literal `policy/repos.toml` occurs anywhere in any `run` string in the targets job. The actual resolver can hardcode its enabled repository list while an unrelated step, dead branch, comment, or no-op retains that literal, and the marquee one-source-of-truth assertion stays green. The supplied mutant only replaces the sole current occurrence, so it does not exercise this mutually masking/decoy case.
issues.fix_hint: Bind the finding structurally to the exact step that owns `id: resolve` and prove that this executable step parses the policy and emits its derived enabled set. Add a decoy mutant that hardcodes the resolver while retaining `policy/repos.toml` elsewhere; the shipped assertion must fail.
issues.title: Policy sourcing is proven by a vacuous cross-step substring

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The new seam coverage does not yet enforce the full executable resolver path it claims to protect. In particular, a valid `if: false` mutation can disable the resolver while every added check and every mutant-table row remains green. The policy-source finding is also only a broad substring test across all target-job steps, so it can be satisfied by dead or unrelated text while the actual resolver is hardcoded. These are fail-silent YAML-seam survivors on the marquee trust-plane behavior, so this round requires changes.
